title: Interior Department Cancels Automatic ESA Protections for Newly Listed Threatened Species
detail: The US Fish and Wildlife Service finalized a rule rescinding the Endangered Species Act's 'blanket 4(d) rule,' which had automatically extended the same take prohibitions given to endangered species to any newly listed 'threatened' species. Effective for species listed or reclassified after August 20, 2026, imperiled species will instead require individualized, species-specific 4(d) protection plans — a potentially lengthy process during which companies can seek exemptions for oil and gas drilling, mining, and other development. A companion rule requires economic-impact analysis when designating critical habitat. About 30 species currently proposed for threatened listing — including monarch butterflies, alligator snapping turtles, and California spotted owls — would be affected. Interior Secretary Doug Burgum said the ESA had been 'used for too long to stop almost any new project in America, driving up costs for families.' The Center for Biological Diversity filed a federal legal challenge, with attorney Noah Greenwald warning: 'If you're exempting certain industries that cause habitat destruction, in many instances you'll be exempting the main threat to those species.' FWS previously eliminated the same blanket rule in 2019 before it was restored in 2024.
